## Verdict: REJECT (one checklist FAIL on acceptance criterion 22)

The PR is not ready to merge, because the internal Windows install runbook asks the AC/DC sample question without stating the expected answer of 2 albums, which criterion 22 requires of every first-run walkthrough.
Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

- VC-95: FAIL (critical) — Each first-run walkthrough lists Docker with Compose and an Anthropic API key as prerequisites. It starts the `examples/mysql-demo` container and points SQL Lens at it through a `mysql+pymysql://` URL. It keeps the Chinook sample questions, and wherever it asks the AC/DC question it states the expected answer, 2 albums. The walkthroughs are, at minimum: - the README quick start; - step 2 of `docs/external/getting-started.md`; - the fast path and the manual install in `docs/external/install-claude-desktop-windows.md`. Where these pages explain connecting to the reader's own database, they say SQL Lens needs a MySQL 8.0+ server. The README quick-start heading, the getting-started introduction and `docs/external/index.md` no longer promise a 60-second or under-a-minute first run. Any first-run duration they state includes pulling the `mysql:8.0` image and loading the demo. [README.md] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json read; criterion 22 present and usable. Most named walkthroughs conform: README.md:18-33 (Docker+Compose, Anthropic key, mysql:8.0 pull 'a few minutes', mysql-demo compose, mysql+pymysql URL, AC/DC 'The answer is 2', MySQL 8.0+ for own DB); docs/external/getting-started.md:3,8-9,26-40,56-58 (expected 2 albums),96; docs/external/install-claude-desktop-windows.md:11-14,22-31,70 (expected answer 2 albums),76,129; docs/external/index.md has no duration promise. No 60-second/under-a-minute first-run promise remains in those. However docs/internal/installation/claude-desktop-windows-install.md is a parallel Windows first-run walkthrough (fast path lines 16-28, manual install 116-133, mysql-demo, mysql+pymysql) and at line 69 it asks the AC/DC question ('New chat: "Using sqllens, how many albums did AC/DC release in the chinook database?"') without stating the expected answer of 2 albums; lines 66-71 contain no such statement. Criterion: 'wherever it asks the AC/DC question it states the expected answer, 2 albums'. This is a departure. (Only the external pages were fixed; the internal doc's AC/DC line is the same as in base, view-base line 63.)

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)

<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `tests/unit/test_safety.py:1257-1263` (`test_catalog_checks_run_no_scope_analysis`) only checks with `hasattr` that module attributes are gone, so a qualified call to `sqlglot.optimizer.scope.traverse_scope` would still pass it. The schema-only behavior is already covered by `test_is_catalog_table_is_schema_only`. (raised by 1/5 agents)

- VC-8: FAIL (suggestion) — The comment says the vendored Chinook_MySql.sql has CRLF line endings and is byte-identical to upstream. [.gitattributes]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The CRLF part holds: examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql has 15876 lines ending in \r. But the .gitattributes:6 comment also says 'its hash is pinned'. A search of the head view for the file name, 'mysql-demo', sha256 and 64-hex strings across tests/, examples/, docs/, .github/ and LICENSES/ found no recorded hash and no test that checks one. LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt:285-290 only says 'Vendored verbatim from release v1.4.5', with no hash. examples/mysql-demo/README.md has none either. The authored comment therefore states a hash pin that does not exist. I could not check byte-identity to upstream without network access, but the missing pin alone makes the comment wrong. The claim also says the file is byte-identical to upstream, and nothing in the repo verifies that.

  </details>

- VC-17: FAIL (suggestion) — configuration.md says `--check-db` opens and immediately closes a connection to `database.url`. [docs/external/configuration.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  docs/external/configuration.md:348 says --check-db 'Opens and immediately closes a connection to database.url.' probe_database (src/sqllens/preflight.py:105-109) also, when cfg.rule_sets.loaded is not None, runs _check_rule_set_catalog on the open connection, reading information_schema via check_catalog and raising PreflightError on a missing table/column or failed read (lines 117-140), and marks the catalog confirmed. The function's own docstring (54-66) says so. The configuration.md row omits this, so a rule-set user is not told --check-db can fail for catalog mismatch or information_schema privileges. docs/external/rule-sets.md:352 (unchanged in base and head) says --check-db 'repeat[s] the check that blocked startup', i.e. the catalog check, contradicting the 'only opens and closes' description. Without a rule-set file the description is accurate.

  </details>

- VC-49: FAIL (suggestion) — The probe_database docstring says the remaining probes are non-mutating and the connect timeout bounds startup; a non-MySQL scheme raises PreflightError. [src/sqllens/preflight.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Verified parts: (1) Non-mutating holds: probe_database (preflight.py:54-114) only connects, and with a rule-set file calls check_catalog (rule_sets.py:1118-1148), which executes two SELECTs on information_schema and closes the cursor; no writes or commits, and read_only is not consulted. probe_llm, probe_auth do no writes. (2) A non-MySQL scheme raises PreflightError('database','unsupported database scheme (expected mysql)') at preflight.py:111-114. Counterexample to the 'connect timeout bounds startup / a wedged host can't extend startup indefinitely' sentence (preflight.py:63-66): pymysql.connect at preflight.py:98-100 is given only connect_timeout=5, no read_timeout or write_timeout (contrast rule_sets.py:1221-1226, which sets both for the request-time check). With a rule-set file configured, _check_rule_set_catalog -> check_catalog runs cursor.execute/fetchall on that connection, so a server that completes the handshake and then stalls the information_schema read blocks startup indefinitely. The docstring's claim is therefore overbroad for the rule-set path. Limited reach (stalling after a successful handshake, rule-set configured), so suggestion.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (8)

<details><summary>8 items</summary>

- VC-28: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — placeholder

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

It has no source_file, source_line, source_excerpt, verify_hint or verify_against, so it states no checkable property and names no subject to read in the head view. No command or file read could settle it.

  </details>

- VC-40: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — During first-start init the mysql:8.0 image runs a temporary server with no TCP listener, so the TCP healthcheck stays unhealthy until init is done and the demo user exists. [examples/mysql-demo/compose.yaml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The claim depends on the mysql:8.0 image's docker-entrypoint.sh (docker_temp_server_start, --skip-networking). No dependency_sources were supplied, the entrypoint script is not in the views, and a filesystem Glob for docker-entrypoint.sh found only unrelated ADR project scripts. I read examples/mysql-demo/compose.yaml:16-31 and confirmed the healthcheck connects over TCP (-h127.0.0.1) as chinook_reader and queries Chinook.Album, so it can only succeed once the data and user exist. I could not read the image script itself, and I did not run docker run mysql:8.0 cat /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh.

  </details>

- VC-50: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — sqlglot's exp.Table.db returns the schema qualifier string (empty for unqualified tables, including table-valued functions in FROM), so is_catalog_table can lower-case it. [src/sqllens/safety/readonly.py:273]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Item has no dependency_sources and sqlglot is not vendored in the views. Globs for **/sqlglot/expressions* under the repo root and / found nothing, so Table.db in sqlglot 30.x (declared sqlglot>=30.22,<31, pyproject.toml:46) could not be read. readonly.py:273 uses (table.db or '').lower(), which tolerates an empty value, but that does not show what Table.db returns. Missing evidence: sqlglot expressions.py Table.db source.

  </details>

- VC-53: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The safety package docstring says the per-runner statement timeout is SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME on MySQL, a server-side time bound. [src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:28]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Docstring at src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:28-29 matches the code in part: sql_runner.py:145-153 runs `SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME = %s` per connection when statement_timeout_ms > 0, and this is a server-side bound. The runner's own comment (sql_runner.py:146-149) says MAX_EXECUTION_TIME only affects SELECTs and is a no-op for other statements. The docstring gives no qualifier, so with read_only=false a non-SELECT statement is not bounded. I found no unchanged file that requires the unqualified wording, and I did not check whether a shipped caller reaches that path with a timeout set. I cannot say whether this is a FAIL or INVALID, so the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE. The overstatement applies only to non-SELECT statements.

  </details>

- VC-69: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — MySQL returns a quoted alias label exactly as written, padding included [tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The comment at tests/unit/test_safety_masking.py:246-248 asserts MySQL returns a quoted alias exactly as written, padding included. That is server behavior (whether the MySQL server trims trailing spaces from a backtick-quoted SELECT alias, as Item::set_name has historically done) and is reported through PyMySQL cursor.description. The repository's code and the tests do not exercise it, and no MySQL server source or PyMySQL source was available or run. Reading the repo cannot settle it. Missing evidence: running `SELECT 1 AS `token_count `` against a MySQL server and inspecting cursor.description.

  </details>

- VC-87: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — `examples/mysql-demo/` holds a `sqllens.toml`, a Docker Compose file, a `README.md`, the user-creation init script and `Chinook_MySql.sql`. `.gitattributes` exempts `Chinook_MySql.sql` from line-ending normalization. Both the committed blob (`git cat-file -p HEAD:examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql`) and the checked-out file have SHA-256 `02a1835417c3ea19bff64e1d1f22be738ce51b3f88b0473c24eebff9a3ccde4b` and are 616,450 bytes. [.gitattributes]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Graded with criteria.json (criterion 14 present, well-formed). Verified: examples/mysql-demo/ in head view holds sqllens.toml, compose.yaml, README.md, demo-user.sql (user-creation script), Chinook_MySql.sql. .gitattributes:7 has `examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql -text`. inventory.json lists Chinook_MySql.sql size 616450 (matches the claim). NOT verified: the SHA-256 02a18354...de4b of the blob and checked-out file; inventory carries only the git SHA-1 blob id (cdbd482f...), and I have no way to compute SHA-256 over the file by reading (no shell run: `sha256sum` / `git cat-file -p HEAD:... | sha256sum` not run). Missing evidence: that hash computation.

  </details>

- VC-89: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — With `SQLLENS_LLM__API_KEY` set: 1. Start the demo container with `docker compose` from a fresh checkout and wait until it is ready. 2. Run `sqllens validate --check-db -c examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml`. It exits 0. 3. Query the demo database as the demo config's user for the number of albums whose artist is `AC/DC`. It returns 2. The demo config keeps `read_only = true`, and its ChromaDB `persist_dir` lies under `examples/mysql-demo/`. A run that cannot use Docker ends Blocked on this criterion. [examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql:257]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 16, so it counts. Static parts verified in head view: Chinook_MySql.sql:257 defines the only AC/DC artist as ArtistId 1; the Album INSERT block (533-~880) has exactly two rows with ArtistId 1 (line 534 AlbumId 1, line 537 AlbumId 4), so the AC/DC album count is 2. examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml:16 keeps read_only = true and :24 persist_dir = ./examples/mysql-demo/chroma. compose.yaml uses mysql:8.0, loads Chinook_MySql.sql and demo-user.sql, healthcheck connects as chinook_reader over TCP to Chinook.Album, so --wait should work, and the toml URL matches that user. Not run: the criterion requires an actual `docker compose -f examples/mysql-demo/compose.yaml up -d --wait`, `sqllens validate --check-db -c examples/mysql-demo/sqllens.toml` (exit 0), and a live count query as chinook_reader. I did not execute these (no Docker/runtime here), and the criterion states a run that cannot use Docker ends Blocked. The static read cannot settle the runtime steps (e.g. 616KB script loading cleanly under MySQL 8.0, demo-user grants), so the claim stays unsettled.

  </details>

- VC-91: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — `LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt` has a section for `examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql`. The section names the upstream project, the v1.4.5 release and its URL, and it carries the upstream copyright line and permission notice verbatim. [LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

Criterion 18 in criteria.json counts (valid list). Whether the copyright line (year range) and permission text are verbatim upstream could not be checked: the upstream LICENSE is not in the views (grep for 'Luis Rocha' finds only this section and the SQL header 'Author: Luis Rocha'), and I did not fetch the upstream v1.4.5 LICENSE. Missing evidence: upstream chinook-database v1.4.5 LICENSE.md text (year range and wrapping).

  </details>

</details>

checklist.evidence: The CRLF part holds: examples/mysql-demo/Chinook_MySql.sql has 15876 lines ending in \r. But the .gitattributes:6 comment also says 'its hash is pinned'. A search of the head view for the file name, 'mysql-demo', sha256 and 64-hex strings across tests/, examples/, docs/, .github/ and LICENSES/ found no recorded hash and no test that checks one. LICENSES/THIRD-PARTY.txt:285-290 only says 'Vendored verbatim from release v1.4.5', with no hash. examples/mysql-demo/README.md has none either. The authored comment therefore states a hash pin that does not exist. I could not check byte-identity to upstream without network access, but the missing pin alone makes the comment wrong. The claim also says the file is byte-identical to upstream, and nothing in the repo verifies that.

The function's own docstring (54-66) says so. The configuration.md row omits this, so a rule-set user is not told --check-db can fail for catalog mismatch or information_schema privileges. docs/external/rule-sets.md:352 (unchanged in base and head) says --check-db 'repeat[s] the check that blocked startup', i.e. the catalog check, contradicting the 'only opens and closes' description. checklist.claim: The probe_database docstring says the remaining probes are non-mutating and the connect timeout bounds startup; a non-MySQL scheme raises PreflightError.
checklist.source_excerpt: The remaining probes are non-mutating: open and
checklist.verify_against: src/sqllens/preflight.py probe_database, probe_memory and the rule-set catalog check
checklist.verify_hint: Trace a config with a rule-set file and read_only=false through probe_database and the other probes; confirm none writes anything.
checklist.evidence: Verified parts: (1) Non-mutating holds: probe_database (preflight.py:54-114) only connects, and with a rule-set file calls check_catalog (rule_sets.py:1118-1148), which executes two SELECTs on information_schema and closes the cursor; no writes or commits, and read_only is not consulted. probe_llm, probe_auth do no writes. (2) A non-MySQL scheme raises PreflightError('database','unsupported database scheme (expected mysql)') at preflight.py:111-114. Counterexample to the 'connect timeout bounds startup / a wedged host can't extend startup indefinitely' sentence (preflight.py:63-66): pymysql.connect at preflight.py:98-100 is given only connect_timeout=5, no read_timeout or write_timeout (contrast rule_sets.py:1221-1226, which sets both for the request-time check). With a rule-set file configured, _check_rule_set_catalog -> check_catalog runs cursor.execute/fetchall on that connection, so a server that completes the handshake and then stalls the information_schema read blocks startup indefinitely. The docstring's claim is therefore overbroad for the rule-set path. Limited reach (stalling after a successful handshake, rule-set configured), so suggestion.

checklist.claim: The safety package docstring says the per-runner statement timeout is SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME on MySQL, a server-side time bound.
checklist.source_excerpt:
* Per-runner statement timeout (``SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME`` on MySQL) —
  a server-side time bound.
checklist.verify_hint: Check the MySQL runner sets MAX_EXECUTION_TIME per session and that it bounds non-SELECT statements the guard lets through when read_only=false.
checklist.evidence: Docstring at src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:28-29 matches the code in part: sql_runner.py:145-153 runs `SET SESSION MAX_EXECUTION_TIME = %s` per connection when statement_timeout_ms > 0, and this is a server-side bound. The runner's own comment (sql_runner.py:146-149) says MAX_EXECUTION_TIME only affects SELECTs and is a no-op for other statements. The docstring gives no qualifier, so with read_only=false a non-SELECT statement is not bounded. I found no unchanged file that requires the unqualified wording, and I did not check whether a shipped caller reaches that path with a timeout set. I cannot say whether this is a FAIL or INVALID, so the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE. The overstatement applies only to non-SELECT statements.
